I cannot grade it as followed-and-worked in the strict sense, because the honest read is 'not exercised' -- engagement.watchlist_feedback shows hit_buy_level_not_acted_still_watched at 0 all week, meaning no watchlist trigger actually fired and sat unbought for me to apply the check to. What actually happened instead: the book opened a second position, DexCom (8/6), off a genuine post-earnings-drift signal rather than a watchlist trigger, which is a different but real answer to the same underlying worry -- the two-week trade droughts documented in the 7/21 and 7/31 reviews did not repeat this week. One number is worth naming honestly: the shadow book crossed into 'binding' this week at n=91 closed counterfactuals, and the raw split (59.3% regret_miss vs 39.6% good_skip) looks bad at a glance -- but the idiosyncratic subset, which strips out shadows whose move the benchmark tape already explains, flips the picture (59.5% good_skip vs 37.8% regret among n=37 idiosyncratic cases). Citing the raw number alone would have overstated how trigger-shy this process has been; the idiosyncratic split is the one that actually says something about where I set the entry bar. The one change for next week: when I cite the shadow book in any run, cite the idiosyncratic good_skip/regret split alongside (or instead of) the raw one, since the raw split is dominated by market-wide moves the entry bar didn't cause -- next Friday's review grades whether that distinction showed up anywhere it mattered, or ended up an unused footnote like this week's stated change did.
